title: Set a plug-in lamp timer: with a pen, push down only the 6:00-10:30 PM segments, 3.3 mm apart, then turn it to the time
instruction: It is 2:30 PM. Set the plug-in timer so the lamp comes on at 6:00 PM and goes off at 11:00 PM: with the pen, push down the ten segments from 6:00 PM to 10:30 PM and no others, and turn the dial clockwise until its pointer shows 2:30 PM.
context: Plug-in 24-hour timers switch lamps, fish-tank and holiday lights on and off; police advise putting a lamp on one when the house is empty, and the mechanical kind costs about $8. You push down the segments for the hours the lamp should be on, then turn the dial clockwise to the time now; the maker's sheet suggests pushing them with "the tip of a pen or pencil". Its 48 segments, one per half hour, sit 3.3 mm apart, half a fingertip's thickness, round a 52 mm dial. The robot takes the pen from the mug and clicks down the ten segments from 6:00 to 10:30 PM, leaving the 5:30 and 11:00 PM ones beside them up; catching either sets the lamp half an hour wrong (0.5). Unlike a pin guided by its hole or a key pressed with a fingertip, nothing guides the pen: the 1 mm ball at the end of a 150 mm pen must land within 1.3 mm of each segment's centre and push about 3 N through the click without skidding onto the next. A gripper pushing a segment down caps the score at 0.25.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Power strip: a white 6-outlet power strip, its outlets in a row and an on/off switch at one end, switched off, 280 x 50 x 38, 0.4 kg. It lies flat, sockets up, its length along y and its switch end toward the robot's right, centred at x 300, y 5; its cord runs straight back off the table. Timer: a GE 24-Hour Plug-In Mechanical Timer, model 15119 (white plastic, listed 2.4 x 2.4 x 2.3 in, 3.2 oz), plugged into the strip's third socket from the switch end, dial up, centred at x 300, y 0. Its top edge, with the OUTLET ON / TIMER ON slide switch at TIMER ON, faces +x, so the pointer on the dial's fixed white centre points away from the robot; its own outlet faces +y. Dial: black, on a ribbed side 52 across standing 8 proud of the timer's face. Round its top edge are 48 segments, one per half hour, each 3.0 wide with 0.3 gaps (3.3 apart) and 5 long; up, a segment stands 2 proud of the dial with its top 80 up; pushed down it is level with the dial. Hours 1 to 12 are printed twice, a sun at noon and a moon at midnight, with 6:30 PM to 6:30 AM on a black band. Start: every segment up, the pointer at 9:00 AM. Lamp: an IKEA LAMPAN table lamp (white plastic, 290 tall, 130 base, 190 shade) with a 470 lm LED bulb, its own switch on, at x 550, y 300; its cord runs behind the strip to the timer's outlet. Pen: a used-up BIC Round Stic ballpoint (1.0 mm ball, cap off, ink run out so it leaves no marks), 150 long, 8 across, 5 g, standing point down in a ceramic mug (95 tall, 80 across, 0.3 kg, handle to the robot's right) at x 220, y -200, its top leaning on the mug's near rim, toward the robot. Estimates: strip size and mass, dial and segment sizes, travel and heights, pen size and mass, mug size and mass. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run. In simulation, read every 50 ms step from the segment, dial and switch joints and the arms' and pen's poses. In a real trial, a phone photo of the dial taken from 45 degrees above decides the score (a raised segment stands 2 mm proud); then the lamp test confirms it: switch the strip on and turn the dial one full turn clockwise by hand, noting the pointer each time the lamp goes on or off. Without a 120 V supply, a continuity tester between the unplugged timer's narrow blade and its outlet's narrow slot stands in for the lamp. Down: a segment pushed fully down, level with the dial; one left part way down counts as up. Time set: the pointer between 2:15 and 2:45 PM, the dial turned clockwise only (turned back counterclockwise more than an hour, 15 degrees, at any time: not set). Every score needs, held for 1 s at the end: both grippers and the pen at least 20 mm from the timer, the slide switch still at TIMER ON, and the timer fully in its socket (never raised 3 mm). A gripper seen pressing a segment's top as it moves down, at any time (trial video; in simulation 0.5 mm or more, or a click), caps the score at 0.25; a touch that does not push one down, such as fingers on the segments' ends while turning the dial, does not. 1.0: exactly the ten segments 6:00 to 10:30 PM down and no others (the lamp lights at 6:00 PM, goes out at 11:00 PM and stays out the rest of the day), and time set. 0.75: the same ten and no others; time not set. 0.5: one unbroken run of down segments that is the ten with one end moved by one segment (on at 5:30 or 6:30 PM, or off at 10:30 or 11:30 PM), the other end right, nothing else down. 0.25: at least 8 of the ten down and at most one other. 0: anything else, including nothing pressed or the timer pulled out of its socket.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (3 minutes at 20 Hz), about twice the 1,988-step demo
reset_notes: Switch the strip off. Push every down segment back up by hand, turn the dial clockwise until the pointer shows 9:00 AM, check the slide switch is at TIMER ON and the timer is pushed fully into its socket, and stand the pen point down in the mug, leaning on its near rim, with the mug on its mark. Nothing is consumed; about 1 minute.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX at 480 Hz. Strip, timer, dial and 48 segments are one free articulation; the timer is fixed in its socket. Each segment is a 2 mm slide (5 g for the solver): task.py holds it up with a spring and latches it down once pushed 1 mm (3 N); pushing it back up is not modelled. Dial drag: stick-slip in task.py (0.03 N m). Slide switch: two sprung stops in task.py. No motor or contacts: the score reads the joints. Lamp and cords are visual. Estimates: these forces. Demo reads object poses.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,600 steps; its right arm reached the pen's mug and nudged and turned it slightly, but the pen stayed in the mug and the timer was never touched); demo: 1.0
